datasets: WMT 2020 QE shared task training set

Word-level quality estimation for machine translation output

quote: F1 scores...and we measure...the final quality of the translations in terms of TER...
TER was used because of its popularity as an automatic translation quality metric, and because it counts edit operations and therefore reflects PE effort.
We measure per condition edits done and the final quality of the translations in terms of TER by comparing the post-edited version of the translation to the reference.

The prototype was evaluated by non color-blind professional translators and translation students who were working as freelancers on a platform called Upwork Global Inc.
guideline: Participants rated the helpfulness of word-level quality estimation on a 9-point Likert scale after each segment.
Participants rated the helpfulness of the word-level QE on a 9-point Likert scale and indicated visualization preference.

After post-editing each segment, participants had to press confirm, which we used to record the required time. When confirming, we also showed a pop-up asking "Was the word-level quality estimation helpful?" which the participant had to rate on a 9-point Likert scale.
